subject.title: fix: harden Mattermost slash callback auth

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally fail closed for all non-HTTPS Mattermost native slash callback URLs, including existing explicit HTTP and derived local callbacks?
rationale: This changes a protected webhook transport boundary and can break existing Mattermost setups that currently register over HTTP, so code review cannot choose the permanent security/compatibility policy by itself.

options.title: Accept HTTPS-only after proof
options.body: Require a rebase plus redacted Mattermost proof that HTTPS callbacks register and HTTP callbacks fail closed, then merge the plugin-local policy.

options.title: Keep warning-only compatibility
options.body: Reject this PR's fail-closed behavior and leave the linked issue open for a lower-breakage mitigation or documented operator warning.

options.title: Move to private security handling
options.body: Pause the public PR if maintainers want the transport-boundary decision handled through the security advisory process.

recommendation.title: Accept HTTPS-only after proof
recommendation.body: Require a rebase plus redacted Mattermost proof that HTTPS callbacks register and HTTP callbacks fail closed, then merge the plugin-local policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Mattermost monitor and security-adjacent history makes this the best available routing candidate for the HTTPS fail-closed policy decision.
